subject: Clarification on DPA/SCC scope for logs, backups, and prompt retention
messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@acme-corp.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: security-ops@acme-corp.com
Date: 2026-05-10T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Questions on logs/backups/prompt retention for DPA scope

Hi Hannah,

Thanks for agreeing to take a look. As part of our DPA review and SCC assessment I need to confirm how Redwood handles the following for our account and for hosted customers generally:

- What categories of logs are retained (request payloads, system logs, application logs, audit trails)? How long are each retained by default?
- Backups: retention windows for full and incremental backups, encryption at rest practices, and whether backups are covered by the DPA/SCCs.
- Prompt/content retention: are prompts and completion data stored? If so, for how long and under what legal/operational exceptions (e.g., debugging, abuse monitoring)?
- Purge behavior: if Acme requests deletion for a specific customer/account, what is the timeline for deletion from live systems and from backups? Are there service-level options to shorten backup retention?

We have an upcoming audit and need documentation and a short attestation for these items. Can you send the retention policy and any artifacts (SOC 2, DPA) that clarify scope?

Thanks,
Elena Ruiz
Senior Security Engineer, Acme Corp
security-ops@acme-corp.com

Attachment: Acme-questionnaire-excerpt.pdf
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@acme-corp.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, marcus.lin@redwood.com, ava.chen@redwood.com
Date: 2026-05-10T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on logs/backups/prompt retention for DPA scope

Hi Elena —

Really appreciate the clear list. Looping in Marcus (legal) and Ava (security) to provide the formal details and artifacts; Marissa (account lead) will coordinate delivery and any account-level options.

Quick answers while we assemble docs:
- We retain request logs for hosted API by default for 30 days; enterprise Dedicated/Private customers can configure longer or shorter windows under contract.
- Backups used for DR are retained for up to 180 days by default (encrypted, customer data is included in those backups).
- Prompts/completions for Hosted are retained for up to 30 days to support quality and abuse monitoring; customers can opt out or request stricter retention under the DPA.
- Deletion requests: we purge from live systems promptly (within 48 hours) but data may remain in backups subject to the backup retention window; we can commit to expedited rotations for enterprise deals — details below.

We'll send the SOC 2 report and the current DPA, plus a short summary doc with the exact timelines and technical notes.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Security & Trust Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: (will attach SOC2 + DPA in follow-up)
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, marissa.cole@redwood.com, ava.chen@redwood.com
Date: 2026-05-11T08:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on logs/backups/prompt retention for DPA scope

Hi Elena —

Thanks for the patience. Attached are the formal artifacts: Redwood-SOC2-TypeII-2025.pdf, Redwood-DPA-2026.pdf, and a one-page Data-Retention-Summary-2026.pdf that maps the items you asked about to policy language. Key points pulled from those artifacts:

1) Logs
- Request/ingestion logs (headers, timestamps, request IDs) are retained for 30 days by default for hosted customers. Request payloads (prompts) are covered separately (see below).
- Security/audit logs (authentication events, admin activity) are retained 365 days for incident response.
- These retention periods are configurable for enterprise customers via contract.

2) Backups
- Backups for the hosted control plane and customer data snapshots are encrypted at rest (AES-256).
- Retention: incremental snapshots retained 90 days; full backups retained 180 days by default.
- Backups are part of the DPA/contractual scope; Redwood is responsible for encryption and segregation; however, under Private/Dedicated deployments, customers may host backups and control retention.

3) Prompt and completion data
- Hosted API: prompt and completion text is retained for up to 30 days for quality, abuse monitoring, and routing optimizations.
- Customers may opt out of prompt retention via account settings or contract terms (opt-out flag and API parameter).
- For Dedicated/Private deployments, prompt retention is under customer control and can be configured to 0 days (no retention).

4) Deletion and purge timelines
- Live system deletion: once a deletion request is accepted, active records are removed from live indexes and stores within 48 hours.
- Backup purge: data in backups will be removed on backup rotation schedules; in the default configuration that can be up to 180 days. For enterprise customers we can negotiate an accelerated rotation (e.g., 30–60 days) documented in the SOW.
- Legal holds: preservation for litigation can override deletion timelines; customers will be notified.

We can provide an attestation letter for your audit stating these standard defaults and any account-specific adjustments we agree to. Let me know if you need a named contact for a DPA amendment and whether you want us to propose a shorter backup retention for Acme.

Regards,
Marcus Lin
Head of Legal, Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood-SOC2-TypeII-2025.pdf; Redwood-DPA-2026.pdf; Data-Retention-Summary-2026.pdf
From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@acme-corp.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, marissa.cole@redwood.com, security-ops@acme-corp.com
Date: 2026-05-11T10:46:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on logs/backups/prompt retention for DPA scope

Marcus/Hannah —

Thank you, that helps a lot. Two follow-ups:
1) For our audit we need a short written attestation that backups (full + incremental) are included in the DPA scope and that they are encrypted at rest. The attestation can be a one-paragraph statement and a contact for escalation.
2) We want an option to set prompt retention to 0 days for our production Org in Hosted. Is that possible immediately, or does it require a contract amendment? If it is immediate, please provide the API/account setting and any limitations (e.g., data may still be present in backups).

If you can send the attestation and the exact account configuration steps, we can fast-track the audit.

Thanks,
Elena

Attachment: audit-checklist.csv
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@acme-corp.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, marcus.lin@redwood.com, ava.chen@redwood.com
Date: 2026-05-12T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on logs/backups/prompt retention for DPA scope

Hi Elena —

Quick update and next steps:
- Attestation: attached is a one-paragraph attestation confirming that backups (full and incremental) are included in the DPA and are encrypted at rest (Redwood-SOC2-TypeII-2025.pdf and Redwood-DPA-2026.pdf attached). Marcus is the escalation contact (marcus.lin@redwood.com).
- Prompt retention opt-out: we can enable prompt retention = 0 for your org immediately on the hosted platform. Implementation notes:
  * API/account flag: data_retention.opt_out = true (we will send the exact API call and a short script).
  * Effect: new requests will not be persisted for quality/abuse monitoring; note that any previously captured data remains subject to backup retention until rotation.
  * Timing: change applies immediately to new traffic; propagation to all systems within 24 hours.
- Backup rotation: we can offer an accelerated rotation to 60 days for backups for Acme under an SOW amendment; if you need 30 days we will escalate to execs for approval.

Action items we will execute this week:
1) Send the signed attestation and the API script to perform opt-out.
2) Marissa will follow up to record the SOW amendment option for backup retention.
3) Ava will schedule a brief technical call to walk your engineering team through the opt-out and confirm monitoring tradeoffs.

If that all sounds good I will have the docs and script to you within 24 hours.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Security & Trust Operations, Redwood Inference
